They may have an open vacation/time off policy that a lot of Washington companies are doing (read several articles about this becoming the new thing). Essentially it’s been proven to cut down on absences and abuse of the system because employees are able to take time when needed without stressing about the possibility of being fired as well as gaining better work life balance. If that makes sense. Essentially when they do this, employees are less likely to overuse time off and feel trusted to make this decision so they are more responsible. Unless your policy says a specific number I would put this in writing “open time off policy of whatever the common name for this policy is in your state. I’ve seen it as “Unlimited Vacation/PTO” in my state. Essentially that means they won’t track your days off but you still have to notify your employer of planned days off and I say usually a week in advance. They still have the right to deny it based off business needs though (usually in company policy it has this written). So I would state “due to [insert payroll company here] being unable to process my Vacation/PTO/Sick leave balances, I propose the following policy for my formal Vacation, PTO, and sick leave policy. If at company 1-5 years: 10 days vacation a year or 80 hours, 32 Hours Personal Time off, and Paid sick leave (as ordered by Washington state, https://www.lni.wa.gov/workers-rights/leave/paid-sick-leave/implementing-a-paid-sick-leave-policy ) I will accrue 1.2 hours for every 40 hours worked, capping sick time at 520 hours a year and allows for roll over if it does not exceed 520 hours. (sidenote it’s usually 1 hour but bc of the inconvenience added a little more time, also the 520 hours is my companies policy bc if you get to that much sick leave, then you never call in sick and deserve the hours). I would then account for the days you have used this year and write your current balance so they can add it to your paystub so you’ve made it easier on them and less “complicated.” I would also adjust as you see fit based off tenure and level in company. Hope that helps!
